newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds up, some new junk up two pts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds up, some new junk up two pts.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds were boosted with U.S. Treasuries into mid-session following a shot of soft economic data, and spreads tightened in spots, dealers said.

Bullish tone set the scene for 1/4 point to 1/2 point gains in the broad high-yield market, meanwhile. New junk issues outpaced other paper when freed-to-trade, traders said, as they have for the past two weeks.
Fixed-income markets rose after the Commerce Department said orders for durable goods fell 3.1 percent in August against forecasts for a decline of 0.1 percent.
The U.S. Treasury benchmark 30-year bond rose more than 1/2 point after the data and was quoted up 21/32 at 98-13/32 to yield 6.88 percent at 1224 EDT/1624 GMT.

Back in the high-yield arena, dealers reported moderate activity surrounding telecommunication debt and a smattering of new paper. Iron Mountain Inc's $165 million 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced at par on Thursday to yield 10.125 percent, were bid at 102-1/2 out of the gate.
"The market remains technically in wonderful shape, new deals come and could be (poor credits) and it'll trade up strong," said one high-yields trader.

Elsewhere, E&S Holdings Corp's $200 million senior subordinated notes, priced at par to yield 10.375 percent late on Tuesday, was quoted at 102 bid. The bonds rose to a 101-3/4 bid, 101-7/8 offer market on Wednesday.

Telecom paper was up 1/4 to 1/2 point in general, according to one sector trader. Sprint Spectrum zero coupon bonds traded up 3/4 point to 58-1/2 compared with a 57-3/4 bid late Wednesday. Sprint Spectrum's 11 percent debt due 2006 was also higher at 103 bid, 103-1/2 offer.
"This is lagging Treasuries but there's still very good interest," a telecom trader said. "There are better buyers."
